summary.short: Mexican federal statute on telecommunications, broadcasting and satellite services, published in the DOF on 16 July 2025. It creates the regulatory framework for the Comisión and Agencia, spectrum and concession regimes, interconnection and asymmetric rules for dominant or substantially powerful operators, and repeals the Federal Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law. It is not AI-specific.
summary.long: Federal statute published in the DOF on 16 July 2025 that issues the Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión and repeals the Federal Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law. The text is not AI-specific. It declares telecommunications and broadcasting public services of general interest and bans discrimination in their provision (Art. 2), and places spectrum and orbital resources in the public domain (Art. 32). The Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones, a desconcentrated body of the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones, regulates the sectors, sets general rules and may impose sanctions (Arts. 7–10); its five-member Pleno decides listed matters (Art. 12). Title Three sets concession regimes: a single concession for convergent services and spectrum or orbital concessions granted by tender or direct award, with transfer, shareholding notice and extension rules (Arts. 45–101). Title Four covers networks and services: interconnection, number portability, infrastructure sharing, obligations of preponderant or substantially powerful economic agents (Art. 123), network neutrality (Arts. 131–132), public property for deployment and satellite communication. Per the outline, Title Five covers authorizations and Title Six the Public Telecommunications Registry (Arts. 159–181). Title Seven is not described in the outline. The provided excerpt contains the full text of Arts. 1–140; entry-into-force terms are not stated in it.

notes: Part 1 of 3 covers the decree header and Articles 1 to 140 only; relations and entities are limited to these provisions. Registry IDs for cited laws are not known, so target_instrument_id is left empty and target_text names each law. Cross-references under Art. 6 are supplementary-law rules; their legal effect is not analysed here. The repeal is stated in the decree header, not in an article. Part 2 of 3 (Arts. 141 to 298). Relations and entities cover only what this part names. The Comisión and the Agencia appear without full names here. Art. 149 repeats the same item (El canal de transmisión que será utilizado) as fracciones I and II, apparently a drafting duplication. Art. 176 says Sistema Nacional de Información de Infraestructura de Telecomunicaciones, while art. 169 says Sistema Nacional de Información de Infraestructura. Penalty amounts in arts. 280 to 292 are stated as percentages of revenue or in UMA and are not extracted here. Concessionaire, authorised and platform duties are generic classes and are not listed as entities. Section status is schema-required; both sections contain entries above. Part 3 of 3: covers Art. 299 and Transitorios Primero to Trigésimo Segundo, plus the signature block. Most transitional effects depend on the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones plenary being integrated, a date the text does not fix. Vigésimo suspends procedures for fifteen business days and homologation requests for five business days. Trigésimo sets a 120-business-day period for line identification guidelines and Vigésimo Séptimo uses calendar days for its 180-day period. Transitorio Vigésimo Noveno refers to article 114 of 'el presente Decreto', meaning this Law. Publication date DOF 16-07-2025 comes from the page header, not the body of the text.
